articles.title_zh: Nintendo Switch 2 Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition restock live — Target confirms online drop this week
articles.content_orig:
Sales of Nintendo 's flagship Switch 2 plunged in its fiscal second quarter after the Japanese gaming giant rolled out price hikes amid soaring memory costs.
Nintendo said it sold 2.67 million units of the Switch 2 in the three months ended Sept. 30, down 41% from the same period last year. That was also lower than the 3.82 million units sold in the prior quarter.
During the quarter, Nintendo rolled out price increases for the Switch 2 in the U.S., Canada and Japan after hiking the cost of the device in Japan earlier in the year.
Memory, a core component of Nintendo's consoles, continues to face a supply shortage and huge demand, which is driving an unprecedented price surge for the chips.
Still, the Japanese gaming giant stuck to its previous Switch 2 sales forecast of 16.5 million units in the current fiscal year, which ends in March 2027.
Here's how Nintendo did in its fiscal second quarter, compared with LSEG average estimates:
While the Kyoto-headquartered firm has had some strong games this year, including "Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream" and "Pokémon Pokopia", which became a surprise viral hit, there are no major marquee titles.
Investors hope that "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," a remake of one of Nintendo's most iconic games, could boost Switch 2 sales in the coming weeks. The game was released on Thursday.
"Nintendo's only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina Of Time remake. It's not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is," Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games, told CNBC.
"It's getting harder and harder to sell video game hardware these days, and only hits help. Nintendo must step on the gas and deliver more big games next fiscal year to make sure the Switch 2 momentum continues."
Nintendo also has new Pokémon games slated for release in 2027.

articles.title_zh: Ukraine continues strikes on Russian refineries in lead-up to White House meeting
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
US first lady Melania Trump brought Russian and Ukrainian representatives together at the White House on Thursday, calling on both sides to choose "humanity over war" ahead of talks next week in Abu Dhabi.
Kirill Dmitriev, a special envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, attended the rare face-to-face gathering with Ukrainian officials. The event marked a six-day ceasefire that Melania Trump helped negotiate in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which expired on Sunday.
It came as the Trump administration is stepping up efforts to bring an end to Russia's war in Ukraine , which started when Russian troops invaded in early 2022. A trilateral meeting involving officials from the US, Ukraine, and Russia is set for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi.
"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady stated at the event. "We must use the courage we brought to Oleshky to find common ground through a shared concern for the suffering of innocent people," she added.
Melania Trump said she was "involved in every stage of the planning" for the short-term ceasefire, which included reviewing aerial photos and evaluating road and hospital access.
President Trump, who did not attend, praised his wife’s role in the Oleshky ceasefire, remarking to reporters in October that "she does better than our professionals."
Dmitriev was expected to meet US officials while in Washington, according to two people familiar with his plans.
Ukrainian lawmaker David Arakhamia and human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets also attended the gathering. They encouraged the Slovenian-born Melania Trump to maintain her peace efforts.
Both delegations presented the first lady with gifts of appreciation.
Russia’s Dmitriev presented her with a drawing of pink hearts by an Oleshky girl, stating the child "chose to live with her family in Russia," alluding to the dispute over displaced Ukrainian children in Russia. "I love Melania," the artwork stated.
The Ukrainian delegation presented the first lady with a state honor "for your brave heart, for saving our people, and for returning back Ukrainian children."
She provided the visiting delegates with letters addressed to Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The meeting was the first face-to-face contact between Russian and US officials following Tuesday's midterm elections, where Democrats won control of Congress from Republicans, dealing a blow to President Trump.
The incoming Democratic majority starting in January is expected to push for increased aid to Ukraine and scrutinize the Republican president's decisions to arrange a diesel deal with Russia and ease certain Moscow sanctions. Trump has heightened his criticism of Zelensky in recent weeks.
The Kremlin noted it hopes Trump will persist with his peace efforts despite the Republican Party’s loss.
It also stated preparations were under way for a summit between Putin, Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting November 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, China.
Dmitriev previously met Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, at the White House in 2025. Trump's predecessor, Joe Biden, did not invite Russian representatives to the White House.
Dmitriev has assisted in facilitating the release of American detainees in Russia, reuniting Ukrainian children with their families, and supporting the humanitarian effort in Oleshky.

articles.title_orig: IRS announces new federal income tax brackets for 2027
articles.title_zh: IRS announces new federal income tax brackets for 2027
articles.content_orig:
The IRS has announced new federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2027.
In its announcement Thursday, the agency raised the income thresholds for each bracket, which apply to tax year 2027 for returns filed in 2028.
The IRS also increased figures for other key provisions, including long-term capital gains brackets, the estate and gift tax exemption , and eligibility for the earned income tax credit, among others.
For 2027, the top rate of 37% applies to individuals with taxable income above $661,375 and married couples filing jointly earning $793,650 or more.
Here are the federal income tax brackets for 2027:
Federal income tax brackets show how much you owe on each part of your "taxable income," which you calculate by subtracting the greater of the standard or itemized deductions from your adjusted gross income.
The standard deduction will also increase in 2027, rising to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, up from $32,200 in 2026. Starting in 2027, single filers can claim $16,600, a bump up from $16,100.
New federal income tax brackets for 2027 come as Americans wrestle with affordability amid the rising cost of housing , groceries , gasoline and other living expenses.
The consumer price index climbed 3.7% in September 2026 from one year earlier, up from an yearly pace of 3.4% in August, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported in October.
The U.S. federal income tax system is progressive, which means tax rates increase as earnings rise.
For 2027, the federal brackets include seven income tiers, with rates ranging from 10% to 37%. The tax rates apply to each band of income rather than a flat percentage for all earnings.
The IRS adjusts the income ranges for each tax rate yearly based on the consumer price index.
Your federal tax brackets depend on your filing status , which you choose on your tax return. The options include single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse.
You can find your 2025 taxable income on line 15 of your individual federal income tax return, known as Form 1040 .

articles.title_orig: Owners of seized Russian oil tanker claim U.S. improperly sold ship for scrap metal
articles.title_zh: Owners of seized Russian oil tanker claim U.S. improperly sold ship for scrap metal
articles.content_orig:
U.S. authorities sold a seized Russian oil tanker to a maritime scrap dealer for well under market value in an “economically irrational” deal meant to thwart the owner’s bid to recover the vessel, the company lawyers said in court papers.
The Justice Department was ordered to respond to the allegations, made by the ship’s Russian owner, Burevestmarin LLC, by 9 a.m. Friday.
The tanker, Bella 1, was seized by the U.S. military in the North Atlantic in early January after a weekslong chase on the high seas. U.S. authorities said the ship, which they believed was carrying illegal Iranian oil, was caught fleeing an American blockade of Venezuela . Attorneys for Burevestmarin dispute the claim that the vessel was carrying Iranian oil.
The ship was sold to a scrap dealer for $9.1 million, the company’s lawyers said, well below the $21 million that the Bella 1 would fetch as scrap metal alone.
Even a proper scrap metal price tag would understate its worth, they added, because the ship has “substantially greater value” as “an operating commercial vessel.”
“As discussed and previously briefed, the Government posits a world in which it can — while withholding notice to known interested parties and while aware of challenges to the Court’s jurisdiction — engage in precisely this kind of economically irrational sale for its own convenience,”  the owner’s lawyers wrote.
They said the sale was conducted “behind closed doors” as part of the government’s “self-interested and unreasonable decisions.”
Representatives for the Justice Department and the scrap dealer named in court documents could not be immediately reached for comment Thursday.
Previously, DOJ attorneys have argued that seized ships put the government in a financial bind, so selling these vessels is necessary to avoid tens of millions of dollars in maintenance and repair costs.
DOJ attorney Rajbir Datta told the court in July that “the government has spent $60 million in maintaining this and doing all kinds of mechanical fixes to the asset itself.”
A root issue in the ongoing court battle is whether American authorities are right to argue that transporting Iranian oil benefits the sanctioned Islamic Revolutionary Guards Force.
That question is further complicated by the Trump administration permitting international sale of Iranian oil to help relieve domestic fuel prices.
Attorneys representing Bella 1’s owner are also fighting the Justice Department’s efforts to seize other ships that they own, citing what they believe is a legal double standard invoked by the government, court records show.
In the case of the vessel Galileo attorneys for the ship owner argued that “on March 20, 2026, the same day that the Government (under seal and ex parte) alleged that the Galileo was a source of influence over the IRGC and IRGC-QF, it expressly licensed the international sale of Iranian oil — an action that would be illegal under multiple statutes were the shipment of Iranian oil in itself necessarily the equivalent of providing a means of support to the IRGC or IRGC-QF or becoming the property of the IRGC or IRGC-QF.”
In the case of another vessel, Skipper, attorneys for Burevestmarin LLC said the Justice Department did not establish the correct venue and may have improperly seized that vessel. The Skipper was on the “high seas” thus meaning it was outside of the U.S. or a foreign country’s territorial waters.
Tom Winter is NBC’s National Law Enforcement and Intelligence Correspondent.

articles.title_orig: McDonald's plans new value menu offerings next year to boost sluggish sales
articles.title_zh: McDonald's plans new value menu offerings next year to boost sluggish sales
articles.content_orig:
A ‘Barron’s Roundtable' panel discusses how the fast-food chain will manage the pinch to consumers wallets.
McDonald's is testing new value menu offerings with an eye toward launching a new national value menu program in early 2027.
The fast-food giant has sought to counter slowing traffic in the U.S. as the company's quarterly earnings release on Wednesday revealed comparable sales in the U.S. declined 0.2% in the third quarter.
McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski said during the company's most recent earnings call that, in the last week of October, McDonald's began an eight-week test of two new everyday affordable price menu constructs across all day parts at about 1,900 restaurants in a handful of regions.
The test involves mix-and-match bundles to give customers greater choices that are similar to prior buy one, add one offers, as well as fixed bundles with a set combination.
MCDONALD'S TO SPEND $8.5B ON REVAMPING RESTAURANTS, TECH AND FRANCHISE SUPPORT
The McDonald's CEO added that a group of franchisees representing about 4,000 restaurants are moving forward with similar entry-level bundles in advance of the formal test results. Kempczinski said the two groups together "represent more than 40% of the U.S. system, reflecting strong alignment around the opportunity."
McDonald's is planning to roll out a new value menu push early next year after it assesses the results of tests to close out this year. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
"We use the results of this test to determine which structure resonates most with customers, works best operationally and delivers sustainable incremental traffic and sales for franchisees," Kempczinski said. "Our goal is to launch a new program nationally in early 2027.
"Our goal is straightforward. Customers should see a clear and compelling value proposition every time they consider McDonald's, whether they're looking for an affordable individual item, a complete meal or a digital offer in the mobile app."
MCDONALD'S SAYS US SALES SLOWED AFTER VALUE DEAL PUSH FELL SHORT
McDonald's CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company wants to provide a clear value proposition for customers considering the fast-food giant. (McDonald's Corporation)
The value menu plans come after McDonald's in September announced a multi-year plan called "NEXT" that will focus on upgrading restaurants and staff training, as well as deploying technology.
The company will spend $8.5 billion as part of the NEXT strategy through 2036, with about $5 billion of that spending provided through 2030. The NEXT partnering support for franchisees will include a combination of capital support and rent relief.
MCDONALD'S SHAKES UP FALL COFFEE LINEUP AS PUMPKIN SPICE SEASON HEATS UP
McDonald's global CFO Ian Borden said on the earnings call that the fast-food chain is already putting elements of the NEXT strategy into action, including rolling out a new beverage platform , starting the "Make It Golden" training initiative, and setting up operational pilots for hand-breaded chicken.
Borden added that the company is starting to open remodeled NEXT restaurants around the world, including the first international restaurant in Poland.

The company will begin remodeling hundreds of U.S. restaurants in 2027 to revise kitchen layouts and equipment to support future menu changes. McDonald's aims to ramp up to a global run rate above 5,000 restaurants per year in 2028.

articles.title_orig: How Melania Trump Became a Dark Horse Diplomat on Ukraine
articles.title_zh: How Melania Trump Became a Dark Horse Diplomat on Ukraine
articles.content_orig:
Residents who were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as part of a U.S.-brokered temporary ceasefire crossed into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday.
The civilians traveled by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus, following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump .
Oleshky is a city in Ukraine's southeastern Kherson region occupied by Russia since the first days of the Ukraine-Russia war . It is one of the most dire humanitarian crises of the conflict.
The ceasefire began at 3 a.m. Tuesday and is expected to continue through Sunday evening.
The estimated 2,000 remaining residents of Oleshky were offered the choice of traveling to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished food and medical supplies.
Those who chose to return to Ukraine were taken to the Russian city of Anapa, then flown to Homel in Belarus, from where they proceeded back home.
Ukrainian authorities imposed restrictions on disclosing the number of evacuees or the border crossing location. The measures are to safeguard those who chose to remain in Oleshky as well as to protect future humanitarian missions, the organizers said.
Relatives waited on Saturday at the Ukrainian-Belarusian border, along with aid tents, coffee stands and even provisions to feed the pets the evacuees were bringing with them. Volunteers from organizations including the Red Cross, Doctors Without Borders and the World Central Kitchen were also there.
Liza Paliy, 19, who last saw her father over 2½ years ago when she, her mother and sister fled from the occupied territory while he stayed behind, was among those waiting.
"We thought at that time that it would be a month, two maximum, and we would return, but unfortunately, two years have already passed," she said.
Daria Pavlyn also waited at the border in hopes of reuniting with her father, Mykhailo, whom she had not heard from in about a month.
He had planned to flee occupied territory with his family after a nearby strike killed two neighbors but stayed behind when arrangements to care for the family's home and animals fell through.
"We realized that, well, there was no (other) way, and he walked us to the road and that was it — that was the last time" they saw him, Pavlyn said.
She said that since then, he had feared making the arduous journey out, particularly without Russian documents.
Russia and Ukraine have not specified how many people chose to leave the city, but the U.S. first lady posted on social media Friday that the humanitarian convoy could safely evacuate more than 750 people.
Apart from Melania Trump, Pope Leo XIV — the first American pontiff — also pressed Russian and Ukrainian leaders to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.
Fighting has continued elsewhere during the localized ceasefire.
A Ukrainian drone attack killed a 30-year-old woman and a 41-year-old man in Russia's western Bryansk region, local Gov. Yegor Kovalchuk said Saturday. Another five people were wounded, he said.
Local officials also reported Ukrainian drone attacks in the Russian republic of Bashkortostan. Russian media outlets said there was a fire in the region's capital, Ufa, home to several oil refineries.
Russia's Ministry of Defense said Saturday its forces had shot down 433 Ukrainian drones overnight.
Zelenskyy said Moscow launched drone attacks on energy and railway infrastructure across Ukraine overnight, leaving 280,000 households in the Dnipro and Kyiv regions without power.
The attacks targeted combined heat and power plants in the Kyiv and Sumy regions, four electricity substations and a gas distribution facility in the Dnipro region and railway infrastructure in Dnipro and Kharkiv, he said, adding that repair crews were working to restore power.
Aidan  Stretch contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
articles.title_zh: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — A wave of bomb threats against passenger airliners caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest of such incidents this week that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways.
No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the security threats made against at least 14 airliners. But the threats have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports.
The threats against two flights that landed in Rome came by email that said it was made in opposition to “your feminist regime,” the airport confirmed to NBC News. Italy’s prime minister is a woman, Giorgia Meloni, who has conservative views.
One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus Flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French air force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crewmembers were evacuated while a bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement.
From there, reports of threats in the skies over Europe arrived at dizzying pace, triggering searches by cabin crews and then again by airport security once on the ground.
Security operations were launched at airports in Prague, Copenhagen and Warsaw, with passengers at the last seeing the military and police sniffer dogs patrolling the tarmac.
“It is too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked,” Apostolos Tzitzikostas, European commissioner for sustainable transport and tourism, told a news conference in Brussels.
British Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander appealed for calm, telling Sky News that “we have established processes for dealing with hoax and malicious threats, and that’s what these threats have been.”
A Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted by Italian air force jets to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport “following anonymous reports of a suspected bomb threat,” according to a spokesperson for the city’s airport authority. Bomb disposal experts found nothing.
“Unfortunately, air traffic is sometimes subject to threats, as we have seen this week, when other airlines in Europe have also faced hoax bomb threats,” a Finnair spokesperson, Stiina Tuunanen, told NBC News in an email. “Threats are almost always unfounded.”
That was also the case for another Finnair flight from Helsinki to Vienna, whose threat was found to be baseless after landing safely in the Austrian capital.
LOT Polish Airlines said two of its aircraft from Warsaw were targeted, one flying to Brussels and the other to Paris.
Back on the ground in Warsaw, Polish resident Matthew Bojarsky, 28, was about to fly to Paris for a romantic trip with his American girlfriend, but saw police, military and sniffer dogs on the tarmac, he told NBC News. Passengers were told that “safety protocols” meant their flight, LOT LO331, had to be aborted and moved to a later time.
Elsewhere, three Ryanair flights were interrupted as they headed to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. Two flights, from Copenhagen and Milan, landed at their destination while a third, from London, was diverted to the city of Plovdiv, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said in an email.
Ryanair did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
In the Czech Republic, meanwhile, police said they had received threats about improvised explosive devices being place on four planes heading to the country’s capital, Prague.
In this instance it appeared that at least some of the threats were sent by email, so “clearly there must be a process whereby airlines distinguish more credible threats from obvious hoaxes,” Peter Neumann, a professor of security studies at Kings College London, said.
Thursday’s incidents follow days of airline bomb threats that have forced multiple flights to divert and an airport in Poland to briefly close. No explosive devices were found in the earlier incidents, according to authorities in various countries.
On Tuesday, a security operation was also launched at the Greek island port ⁠of Syros after a bomb threat ​to an Israel-bound cruise ship. Authorities said an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to ⁠the hull of the Panama-flagged Crown Iris that was due to sail ⁠to Haifa.
Authorities have not indicated who could have been behind the incidents and there were no claims of responsibility.
Alexander Smith is a senior reporter for NBC News Digital based in London.

articles.title_orig: Avigdor Liberman drops veto on haredi parties in coalition, opposition in talks with UTJ
articles.title_zh: Avigdor Liberman drops veto on haredi parties in coalition, opposition in talks with UTJ
articles.content_orig:
Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman has dropped his veto on forming a government with haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties, opening the door for the opposition bloc to begin discussions with United Torah Judaism (UTJ), N12's Amit Segal reported on Thursday
The bloc is reportedly discussing the possibility of drafting a more lenient military conscription law, and the current assumption is that Shas would be forced to support the move as well, under pressure from Rabbi Lando.
UTJ , a longtime coalition partner of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , declined to recommend a candidate for prime minister to President Isaac Herzog during the party's consultation earlier on Thursday.
UTJ's decision to abstain came amid reported tensions between the haredi party and Netanyahu, and it benefits the opposition bloc seeking to replace him. Opposition party leaders have recently signaled greater openness to including haredi parties in their coalition.
A potential coalition led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot and including United Torah Judaism (UTJ) would hold 55 seats in the Knesset, falling short of the 61-seat majority needed to form a government. However, it would reduce Netanyahu's bloc to just 46 seats, potentially allowing Eisenkot to form a minority government with Ra'am and the Joint List abstaining.
Yisrael Beytenu denied the report in a statement to The Jerusalem Post .
"We are not aware of any such thing. Nothing has changed since the briefing was given," the party stated.
During the Monday briefing, Liberman ruled out joining a unity government with Netanayhu, along with the option of a minority government that would be reliant on support from the Arab parties. However, his stance regarding joining a coalition with  Shas and UTJ appeared to be more lenient.
Liberman stated that whoever would accept his set of principles and a conscription law to draft the haredim, he would "have no problem with."
Liberman has repeatedly ruled out joining a government with haredi parties in recent years, citing fundamental disagreements over military conscription and issues related to religion and state. He has previously declared that Yisrael Beytenu would not sit with either Arab or haredi parties, describing them as "non-Zionist elements" and arguing that anyone who refuses military service should be considered an evader.
His opposition to compromising on haredi conscription has also shaped coalition negotiations, most notably in 2019, when his refusal to support a compromise on a military draft law helped derail Netanyahu's efforts to form a government, triggering a political deadlock that led to five elections being held between 2019 and 2022.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street fear gauge jumps most since 'Liberation Day' as AI trade stumbles
articles.title_zh: Wall Street fear gauge jumps most since 'Liberation Day' as AI trade stumbles
articles.content_orig:
Whether it's a referendum on the midterms or just a continuation of a bear market in semiconductors that dates back to the group's peak in June, one thing's clear from the options action Thursday: few traders saw this coming.
That's evident in the surge in Cboe Volatility index (VIX) , which jumped as much as 5.7 points to above 28 about 90 minutes after the opening bell on Thursday. It's the highest reading on VIX since March 31, the day after the S&P 500 bottomed after selling off as tensions between Iran, Israel and the U.S. reached fever pitch.
From its intraday low to high Thursday, VIX moved more than 11 points, the biggest one-day move since April 9. Yet with the S&P 500 down 3%, there's an argument to be made that volatility should be higher. Traders use a rule of thumb that 16 points for the VIX equate to a 1% move in the index.
The S&P 500 was headed for its worst decline since April 2025.
"My data says to de-risk, but my gut says this is a blowout that could create a dip-buying opportunity" said Noel Smith, "I do not see macro stuff causing this, like oil or rates. Those things are relatively unchanged. The tape looks like a liquidation and that's exactly what it is according to what I'm hearing with regards to a hedge fund."
Looking at Wednesday's response to the selloff in semiconductors adds a wrinkle for traders that pointed to a too-calm VIX despite Wednesday's tech-stock wreck. With the VanEck Semiconductor ETF down 3%, it was the first day in market history that the VIX concurrently fell more than 4 points, according to data from the X account "OddStats." As of midday, nearly 800,000 calls traded on the VIX, 3.5 times higher than 30-day average, according to Cboe data.

articles.title_orig: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
articles.title_zh: Paraguay's president is impeached minutes after resigning following a bank collapse
articles.content_orig:
A demonstrator holds a mock U.S. dollar bill depicting Paraguayan President Santiago Peña during a protest against the government and Ueno Bank, which Paraguay's central bank seized amid a solvency crisis, in Asunción, Paraguay, Wednesday. Jorge Saenz/AP hide caption
ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay — Paraguay's lower house voted unanimously Thursday to impeach President Santiago Peña just minutes after he announced his resignation, as the collapse of a major digital bank tied to his government froze millions of people's savings, sent protesters surging into the streets and turned his own party against him.
The 78-0 vote marked a stunning repudiation of Peña by lawmakers from his long-ruling Colorado Party, who joined the opposition in backing his impeachment after three days of demonstrations rocked the capital, Asunción. The vote sends the charges to the Senate, where a two-thirds majority is required to convict the president and formally remove him from office.
The impeachment came as thousands protested for a third day, as they attempt to recoup lost savings, wages and pensions from Ueno Bank, a major digital lender.
Peña, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, announced his decision in a video posted to X as lawmakers debated his impeachment, saying he was stepping down in the interest of "the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions."
Paraguay President Santiago Peña speaks to the media at United Nations headquarters, Sept. 19, 2023. Ted Shaffrey/AP hide caption
The president, who until last year held a stake in a company related to Ueno Bank, expressed contrition but stopped short of accepting responsibility for the banking crisis that has plunged a South American nation long prized by foreign investors for its stability into financial and political turmoil.
"I also want to apologize to the people if I have failed them at any point," he said. "It was never my intention to betray the trust they placed in me."
The extraordinary turn of events set the stage for a transfer of power later Thursday. Congress was expected to formally accept Peña's resignation at 5 p.m., clearing the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to be sworn in as president an hour later. Alliana would serve out Peña's term through August 2028, with lawmakers expected to choose a new vice president.
Ueno Bank, which exploded from an obscure finance company to a household name in less than five years, claimed more than 60% of Paraguay's adults as customers. They are now left scrambling to recoup their savings, government pensions, and, for 7,000 employees impacted by the bank's closure, unpaid wages.
Many Paraguayans are left asking how a bank linked to the president, who until last year had a stake in Ueno's holding company, could grow so rapidly in size and importance despite repeated warnings about its dubious lending practices.
The answer lies in the uncomfortable proximity of Peña's long-ruling Colorado Party to the country's regulators and business elite, a weakness that has endured even as steady economic management and rapid growth made Paraguay a darling of international investors in recent years.
"Santiago Peña and the Colorado Party have stolen all our savings," said Luis Pineda, one of the protesters marching to Congress on Wednesday. "We are fed up with 70 years of plunder."
Soon after winning its banking license in 2023, Ueno seemed to be everywhere in Paraguay. The digital lender, a rebranded version of a decades-old finance company, lured customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries, grew to more than 70 locations, sponsored Paraguay's national soccer team and plastered its name on the country's main stadium.
Government money poured into Ueno's coffers under Peña. He also appointed Carlos Carvallo, president of Financiera Ueno, the predecessor to Ueno Bank, to run the central bank, the agency charged with supervising the digital lender.
As of last month, Ueno reported holding roughly $800 million in public deposits, about a quarter of its total, including money from the state pension and health fund and the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.
Even as retirees' savings and other public money piled up at Ueno, worries were escalating inside the central bank. In June, its inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, reported ABC Color, a leading Paraguayan newspaper. Ueno had extended large sums to companies tied to its owners, beyond what the law allows and without enough collateral to cover the debts if they went bad. On a single day in September 2025, nearly $39 million had gone to three such companies.
Peña repeatedly brushed off the warnings. As recently as last month, he defended Ueno and the central bank's oversight, dismissing the concerns as a smear campaign that was spooking the public.
But on Monday, it all came crashing down. Regulators investigating Ueno's loans to companies linked to its owners found poorly documented lending, the central bank said, as well as expenses the bank had wrongly counted as assets.
Once the books were corrected, Ueno's capital, the cushion banks must keep to absorb losses, fell to less than half the legal minimum. The central bank seized the lender Tuesday and announced plans to move customers' accounts, along with whatever assets still hold value, to other banks before liquidating what's left.
Ueno's app, cards and transfers went dark and its branches locked their doors, leaving desperate depositors lined up outside with no way to cash out their savings. On Wednesday, a rush to open new accounts elsewhere crashed other banks' mobile apps, fueling public panic.
Officials appealed for calm and said they had begun repaying depositors, opening new accounts elsewhere for about 280,000 who had banked only with Ueno.
"The banking system is sound," insisted Pedro Acosta Bernal, appointed interim central bank president Wednesday after Carvallo resigned at Peña's request.
Authorities have detained eight senior Ueno executives, including founder Miguel Vázquez and bank President Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud. Lawyers for several of the detained said they needed time to review the allegations before they could comment.
Hundreds of employees of Ueno Bank and other companies belonging to Grupo Vázquez, the bank's parent conglomerate, protested outside the Labor Ministry on Thursday, demanding severance and unpaid wages with their jobs in limbo and their salaries trapped at the failed bank. A day earlier, hundreds of retirees, depositors, university students and workers flooded the streets of Asunción, the capital.
"We want your head, Peña!" they shouted. Their signs demanded Peña's impeachment, called him "the enemy of savers" and pleaded "Give us back our money." Riot police fired pepper spray and rubber pellets to push back the crowds.
Many demonstrators saw Ueno's collapse not just as the result of risky banking but as a case study in official corruption. Only Venezuela ranks worse in South America on the latest index of perceived corruption from Transparency International, a global watchdog.
"This is yet another assault on honest, hard-working citizens, people whose small savings are the fruit of years of labor," said protester Belarmino Balbuena.
At the national stadium that once bore Ueno's name, the bank's logo had already been scrubbed away. But across the capital, fresh graffiti denounced politicians as thieves.

articles.title_orig: 2 arrested after mushroom gummies given to children on Halloween in Ocean Beach
articles.title_zh: 2 arrested after mushroom gummies given to children on Halloween in Ocean Beach
articles.content_orig:
An 80-year-old man and a 45-year-old man suspected of distributing psilocybin gummies to at least 15 trick-or-treating children in Sunset Cliffs were arrested.
An 80-year-old man and a 45-year-old man suspected of distributing psilocybin gummies, also known as "magic mushrooms" to at least 15 trick-or-treating children in Ocean Beach were taken into custody Wednesday after a a search warrant was served on the home suspected of distributing the psychedelics.
Michael Goff, 80, and Shawn Michael Foster were arrested and booked into the San Diego County Jail. Goff was booked on suspicion of possessing a firearm as a convicted felon, while Foster faces suspicion of possessing both a firearm and ammunition as a convicted felon.
Stream San Diego News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC 7.
No charges were filed in connection with psilocybin-infused gummies but San Diego police said officers discovered an identical bag of psilocybin gummies to those distributed on Halloween in the home during a Wednesday morning search of the home on 2100 block of Sunset Cliffs Boulevard.
Multiple bags of psilocybin-infused gummies were left on a residence's porch Saturday night and were later taken by children between 1 and 6 years old, according to the San Diego Police Department.
Police said the children's parents noticed the suspicious candy packages and, upon inspecting them, suspected they contained controlled substances.
Frank Cary and Cameron Hunter were trick-or-treating with their children and several neighborhood families Saturday night when they made the discovery their children had obtained illicit drugs .
The parents said they were walking just a few yards behind their children when the kids approached a porch with a bowl of what appeared to be candy.
"My 2-year-old went up and grabbed one and started walking away with it in his hand,” Cary told NBC 7. “I noticed the picture had a giraffe and words that looked like they were melting. I took it out of his hand and saw that there was a dosage on the front of it. Five grams, [then I ] flipped it around and read 'psilocybin mushrooms.'”
The parents then confronted the homeowners and later filed a police report with the department, saving the packages of the gummies for law enforcement evaluation, which later tested positive for psilocybin.
NBC 7 San Diego visited the house on Monday and spoke to a man who claimed he lived at the house . The man,  who identified himself as Shawn Barger, disputed the parents' account of the situation. He said his wife had been confused when strangers came to their door and confronted her about the packages.
After the search warrant was served, detectives seized over 2.5 pounds of cannabis, more than 25 grams of crystal methamphetamine, a working digital scale, packaging materials and drug sales ledgers.
An illegally possessed rifle was also located at the residence, along with dozens of rounds of unfired ammunition and a partially assembled pistol.
According to police, a San Diego code compliance investigator responded to the scene to begin a separate investigation into the property's unpermitted living structures.
Anyone with information about the case was urged to contact the Narcotics Unit at 619-531-2468. Tipsters who prefer to remain anonymous can call Crime Stoppers at 888-580-8477.
City News Service contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: China and the Netherlands Discuss Plant Breeders’ Rights, AI and Robotics
articles.title_zh: China and the Netherlands Discuss Plant Breeders’ Rights, AI and Robotics
articles.content_orig:
Protecting new plant varieties and applying artificial intelligence and robotics were central to discussions between Chinese and Dutch industry representatives at the 24th China Kunming International Flower Expo.
Organised by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in China, the dialogues brought together more than 130 breeding experts, business leaders and intellectual property professionals from China, the Netherlands and other countries.
Participants examined policy, breeding technology, judicial protection, financial implications and commercial implementation, with variety rights emerging as a key consideration for breeders entering international markets, according to a press release.
Tsjeard Hoekstra, deputy ambassador at the Dutch embassy in China, emphasised that an internationally aligned variety rights system is a prerequisite for breeders to bring their best varieties to market.
Dutch experts outlined developments in their country’s variety rights protection and regulatory approach. Discussions also highlighted that responsibility for protecting varieties extends beyond breeders to businesses involved in sales and distribution.
Li Shenchong, director of the Flower Research Institute at the Yunnan Academy of Agricultural Sciences, called for greater respect for breeding innovation, standardised variety trading, stronger protection of breeding achievements and deeper cooperation. These priorities form part of China’s Initiative on Innovation and Protection of New Plant Varieties (Flowers).
For breeders navigating the lengthy process from initial selection to commercial launch, a stable protection system helps create the conditions needed to introduce new varieties.
A separate discussion explored the application of AI and robotics in floriculture, with Chinese and Dutch experts sharing practical experience with AI crop models.
Limited land availability has helped drive the Netherlands’ investment in efficient cultivation. Over decades, Dutch greenhouse technology has combined sensors, algorithms and growing expertise to reduce inputs and increase output. AI and robotic systems could accelerate that progress.
Erik Smidt, counsellor for agriculture, fisheries, food security and nature at the Dutch embassy in China, emphasised the importance of trusted partners when doing business in China.
He pointed to more than two decades of cooperation between Dutch and Chinese floriculture businesses as a foundation for combining cultivation expertise with emerging technologies.
Across both discussions, participants identified cooperation as essential to advancing the flower sector, through stronger protection for breeding innovations and technologies that help growers produce more efficiently.

articles.title_orig: Musk has little to show for his record spending on Republican campaigns in US midterms
articles.title_zh: Musk has little to show for his record spending on Republican campaigns in US midterms
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the midterms to support Republican candidates, most to help Ken Paxton defeat Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race.
Talarico won. But it was the other Democrat upsets in the state, for governor and attorney general, that could cause bigger problems for Musk and his Texas-based companies: rocket and AI company SpaceX and electric car maker Tesla.
Not only will he likely face greater regulatory scrutiny, but both candidates took direct aim at Musk and his businesses while on the campaign trail.
“It’s less about the blue wave on the Senate or House side,” said tech analyst Daniel Ives, a SpaceX and Tesla bull, about what Tuesday’s election results mean for Musk. “It’s more with the Texas governor.”
Democrat Nathan Johnson, who is replacing Paxton as Texas attorney general, said in July that, if elected, he would investigate whether SpaceX’s Starlink service was unfairly awarded grants designed to expand rural broadband. The internet service is SpaceX’s most profitable unit.
And Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who unseated incumbent Greg Abbott, made opposition to data centers a major plank of her campaign. She has vowed to put a moratorium on new data center construction. Both Tesla and SpaceX have banked their future success on their AI efforts.
The biggest winners and losers of the 2026 midterm elections
SpaceX is planning major investments in new data centers in the next year, including the massive Colossal 3 to be built just outside of Brownsville, Texas. Unlike a lot of artificial intelligence companies, SpaceX earns a profit from selling time on its servers and cloud platforms to other AI companies. Hinojosa’s proposed moratorium would be a critical blow to its plans.
“I mean, those Texas data center plans are a key part of Musk’s ambitions,” Ives said. He said that’s why SpaceX and Tesla shares fell Wednesday, both dropping more than 3%, even as many other tech stocks rose.
Musk, the world’s richest person with a net worth estimated at about $898 billion, likely won’t sweat the money he lost backing Republicans, or even Wednesday’s decline in value for his shares.
How AI companies spent money on the midterms
The bigger issue for Musk is an increased level of scrutiny, which he noted on his social media platform, X, on Wednesday.
“Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,” Musk wrote, referencing his ultimate ambitions.
Experts say lifting and operating data centers in outer space still face many hurdles. But even if it was possible, SpaceX may have to take off from a spaceport in Louisiana if Texas moves to limit launches.
SpaceX has faced public criticism for the operation of its spaceport, “Starbase,” on Texas’ Gulf Coast. Some residents near the launch facilities have long expressed worries about disruptive sonic booms — which can be as loud as gunshots and register as small earthquakes — and collectively filed a lawsuit this year.
Musk bankrolling group using AI to attack Talarico on AI
SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment about the lawsuit. But Musk has previously downplayed sonic booms, saying in a 2022 post on X that “storms and hurricanes that are far more serious than Starship launches.”
Those resident complaints, however, could find a more sympathetic ear from Hinojosa compared to Abbott. (Hinojosa’s campaign did not respond to questions from CNN about her position on the spaceport.)
Tesla also has a big operation in Texas, and its driverless “robotaxis” only operate in four cities in Texas and three cities in Florida. For comparison, rival Waymo, a unit of Alphabet, operates in 15 cities across the country.
Local governments decide which vehicles, self-driving or otherwise, are allowed on their roads.
“It would it would be a big blow if robotaxis faced more regulation,” Ives said.
Tesla hasn’t listed profits or losses for its robotaxi service. But Musk has made it clear that Tesla’s future is selling rides in its robotaxis, not car sales. And a large part of Tesla’s evaluation is the expectation that its robotaxi service will eventually operate nationwide, Ives said.
Ives also says Hinojosa’s threat to the AI industry goes beyond just SpaceX. Texas is a key to US AI development. The state has the most planned data centers in the country, according to research firm Cleanview, and is second only to Virginia for the number open or under construction.
“Hinojosa is a known anti-data center politician and negative on the AI buildout which makes worries around the future of the datacenter buildout in Texas a real issue for tech investors,” Ives said in a note to investors Wednesday. “SpaceX stock will be under pressure.”

articles.title_orig: France strikes live: largest day of protests in years expected as economy fuels unrest
articles.title_zh: France strikes live: largest day of protests in years expected as economy fuels unrest
articles.content_orig:
• General strike : French riot police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon while scuffles broke out in Nantes and authorities arrested agitators who vandalized a Rennes hotel. But overall, the roughly 200 demonstrations across France on Thursday – attended by an estimated 575,000 people – remained relatively peaceful.
• Widespread disruptions : The strike was organized by L’intersyndicale, the group that represents all of France’s main trade unions. Education, health care, public transportation and other sectors were impacted with many services closed for the day.
• Europe discontent : Anti-government protests have swept across the continent in recent weeks. In Greece , students and teachers gathered in central Athens on Thursday to stress the importance of free public education and protest the rising housing and food costs affecting students.
At least 448 people have been detained during the nationwide protests in France, the country’s Interior Ministry said, though that is a fraction of the estimated 575,000 who took part.
The ministry revised down its count of protesters, from the 600,000 it reported earlier today .
There were about 65,000 protesters in Paris alone, the ministry said.
The marches across the country were largely peaceful and proceeded without major incidents, the ministry said. There were some clashes between police and “groups of radical and far-left activists” in places like Rennes, Nantes, Lyon and Marseille, it said.
Firefighters responded to 86 fires, including one at a school common room that was destroyed in Toulouse, it said. An effigy of a police riot officer was set on fire in Strasbourg.
Hundreds of thousands of people are protesting across France today, but it’s a movement that grew out of protests that happened two months ago.
In September, students and teachers at a high school in the Parisian suburbs went on strike, demanding more staff and resources. Their demands were met and the strike ended – but it lit a spark that soon caught nationwide.
The movement has since swelled into a collective cry of anger, bringing together groups with different grievances, capturing widespread discontent over affordability, perceived government inaction, a growing wealth divide, and a deep desire for social and political change.
No longer confined to students, the movement has drawn in trade unions and yellow vest protesters, who are voicing frustrations over the cost of living and calling for French President Emmanuel Macron to go. The labor unions that have called today’s demonstrations in France are demanding higher wages and pensions.
With so many causes now fueling the protests, the anger is unlikely to subside anytime soon.
And with France heading into a deeply divisive presidential election in April , the stakes are only getting higher.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who is leading in the polls, claimed at the end of October that “legitimate social grievances have, yet again, been held hostage by the far left.” Her hard-left rival, Jean-Luc Mélenchon has repeatedly defended the students’ right to protest.
The skyrocketing cost of living in France is one of the factors driving this wave of protests as anxieties around low wages, high prices and the state of public services explode onto the streets.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will hold a “social conference” with employers and unions next Monday as hundreds of thousands of people participate in protests across the country.
The conference will be aimed at addressing questions around “purchasing power and wages,” the prime minister’s office said in a statement .
Today’s general strike and protests have been organized by L’intersyndicale, the group that represents all of France’s main trade unions.
Place de la Nation, in eastern Paris, is a historic plaza synonymous with protest. Marches often end here, and we’re used to seeing huge clouds of tear gas as protesters clash with police.
But tonight, it’s quite an unusual and arresting sight to see the square so full after dark. A huge mass of people continue to stand still beneath a monument celebrating the triumph of the French Republic.
The protest in Paris was authorized by city officials to wrap up at 7 p.m. local time (1 p.m. ET). But with less than 30 minutes to go, it’s unlikely everyone will be able to disperse quickly.
Although this movement initially began with students protesting the state of the education system, it has morphed into one that includes several other concerns united by a key factor: the poor state of the economy.
Protesters on Thursday said they are anxious about low salaries, which have not kept up with inflation, as well as underresourced public services.
“There is a lot of concern about the future, notably the issues of salaries, public services,” Alice Martinovic, an 18-year-old student participating in the Paris protest, told Reuters.
“I hope in the upcoming elections the candidates will really think about this movement and include the opinions of young people, of students, who are now joined by a lot of other workers.”
Meanwhile, Mehdi Dumontroty, a 45-year-old firefighter also protesting in Paris, told Reuters that “our pay has not kept up with inflation.”
“What happened this summer proves that we were right when we said we needed more resources to deal with the crisis that we faced,” he said, referencing fierce wildfires which swept across southern France amid record-breaking, climate change-fueled heat waves.
Almost 600,000 protesters are on the streets of France today, the country’s interior ministry has just estimated, making Thursday the biggest day of protests since this current wave of unrest began in September.
Earlier today, at 1 p.m. local time (7 a.m. ET), the ministry had estimated that 270,000 people were protesting but that number excluded Paris, where a march began this afternoon.
The ministry is expected to release its final figures later today but, as of now, its current estimates indicate that these demonstrations are not quite as big as the 2023 pension reform protests.
French education minister Édouard Geffray has condemned what he said was a “deliberate act of arson” at a school near the city of Toulouse in southern France.
The minister thanked firefighters and law enforcement officials for helping to “limit the damage” cause by the flames.
“This deliberate act of arson could have had tragic consequences for human life. I condemn it in the strongest possible terms and call on everyone to condemn it unequivocally,” he added, while vowing to hold those responsible to account.
Earlier, France’s interior ministry said the blaze started after fireworks were directed at an office hosting the school’s student services.
Authorities in Rennes said they arrested “several dozen” masked individuals who vandalized a hotel, threw objects at police and “violently attacked” union members who were protesting earlier today.
Photos taken by local media show that vandals smashed the hotel’s glass doors and painted graffiti on windows.
Some masked individuals also tried to erect barricades to block some of the city’s roads, lit fires in garbage bins, and threw heavy pétanque balls – used in a popular French game – at police, authorities added.
Despite violent clashes like this, however, the protests today have largely been peaceful even as they have been attended by hundreds of thousands of people.
As today’s march in Paris got underway, the trade unions were in a jubilant mood. Music blared out as the crowd, dominated by left-wing groups, sang and chanted slogans against the government and the far-right.
A police helicopter buzzed above, but in the confines of the avenue we were walking down, there was little sense of the heavy police presence around the protest.
In the distance, the soaring statue of Marianne – the national symbol of France – got smaller and smaller as the march inched its way forward.
The protest route is packed. The movement of the crowd has been brought to a near stands

articles.title_orig: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
articles.title_zh: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
articles.content_orig:
Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX have plunged as tech and artificial intelligence stocks more broadly plummeted a day after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterms.
Those losses dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index down, which had fallen by more than 5% at one point in early trading.
The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the artificial intelligence (AI) industry following Democrat wins in key data centre states including Texas.
Following the election, some tech leaders have acknowledged they need to improve their communication around data centres and the benefits of AI.
SpaceX shares were down more than 9% in by lunchtime in Thursday trading, while Tesla shares dropped more than 11%.
Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night.
Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.
Shares in chipmakers have been suffering, with AMD dropping more than 14% on Thursday, while Micron shares had dropped by as much as 17% before recovering slightly.
Intel shares are down by more than 7% and shares in Nvidia have fallen nearly 9%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen by 10%.
The stock falls also hit the S&P 500 index, which dropped by 3.8% by lunchtime.
Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets.
"Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said.
"Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction."
Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms.
OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board.
"A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening.
Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick agreed that the industry needed to improve their communication about the benefits of AI.
"I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference.
Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction .

articles.title_orig: Iran War Updates: More ships attacked in Persian Gulf, oil prices rebound slightly after post-midterm plunge
articles.title_zh: Iran War Updates: More ships attacked in Persian Gulf, oil prices rebound slightly after post-midterm plunge
articles.content_orig:
Russian President Vladimir Putin received Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, in Moscow Thursday to discuss strengthening ties between their two countries, including a pipeline to import Russian gas.
Speaking to journalists after their meeting, Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it "an extremely important exchange," according to remarks reported by the Iranian embassy.
"During the meeting with Mr. Vladimir Putin, discussions were held regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran," said Rezaei, Iranian state TV reported.
He noted the aim was to enable Iran "to address its own gas shortages while also facilitating the sale of Russian gas to neighbouring countries."
While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by the war with the United States and Israel.
During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the U.S. and Israel struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spent much of the day on calls with his counterparts from several Middle Eastern countries, including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey.
In total, Araghchi held calls with nine different countries in the Middle East. Few details were shared about what was discussed on the calls, simply nodding to "diplomatic efforts to maintain stability in the region."
Notably, Pakistan was one of those countries involved as they have been very closely involved as mediators in U.S.-Iran peace talks. Araghchi spoke to their foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, on Thursday evening.
Araghchi also spoke to Saudi foreign ministers Faisal bin Farhan and Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, despite accusations of Iranian involvement in attacks on that country by the Houthi militia in Yemen.
President Trump's administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by The Associated Press show.
The court documents unsealed Thursday show the Republican administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians through an unnamed third country, although it was unclear when it intended to do so. The judge in the case ordered the government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country and five days' written notice before any such deportation is carried out.
The documents show the administration maintained contacts with Iranian officials during the war over the removals, specifically for submitting travel documents and figuring out "possible avenues for removal."
"We are at war with a country where the President of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless ... A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors," Judge Ana Reyes said according to the Oct. 15 transcript.
"And what you're telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death."
"Yes, your honor," Justice Department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel said. "The government is executing lawful orders of removal."
The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis took credit for disrupting travel using a drone at King Fahd International Airport on Thursday.
"We targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam using a drone and our operation caused a disruption of air navigation at the airport," Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X.
The city of Dammam, which is located in the oil-rich eastern part of Saudi Arabia, and King Fahd airport have been regular targets for Houthi attacks. Multiple drones have disrupted traffic at the airport this week, according to past announcements.
Two people were killed in a Houthi strike on King Fahd airport on Oct. 22.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its associated strike group will make a port call in Singapore Friday and will not reach the Middle East for at least another two weeks, a U.S. official told CBS News on Thursday.
There are already two carrier strike groups in the region and, which officials say is sufficient firepower to execute any commands issued by President Trump.
Mr. Trump has not signaled yet, in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections, whether he intends to order major new strikes on Iran — an option he kept on the table with repeated statements ahead of Tuesday's voting.
The initial knee-jerk reaction to the U.S. midterm election results faded a bit Thursday.
The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil, considered the international standard, rose 2.2% to $96.70, recovering a chunk of its nearly 9% drop from the day before.
Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal.
Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Thursday in Moscow with Russian President Vladimir Putin to deliver a message from Iran's supreme leader, according to the Iranian government.
They met amid uncertainty over President Trump's next move on Iran in the wake of U.S. midterm election results that represented a major rebuke of his policies, including, he has admitted, the decision to launch the war with Iran alongside Israel more than eight months ago.
Mr. Trump said repeatedly ahead of the Tuesday vote that he had yet to make a decision on whether to order major new attacks on Iran or to agree a deal to end the war, which Tehran has so far refused to do until the U.S. accepts its core demands to end its naval blockade, ensure a halt to fighting on all fronts in the Middle East, and ease sanctions.
During the Rezaei-Putin meeting in Moscow on Thursday, the Russian Foreign Ministry warned Russian citizens against all travel to Iran.
"Given the continued risk of a new escalation around Iran, our recommendations to Russian citizens remain unchanged," ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told reporters in Moscow. "We recommend temporarily refraining from traveling to that country until the situation is resolved. We also ask our compatriots already in Iran to exercise vigilance and avoid crowds, public events, and areas near military and government facilities."
She said the guidance was "based on the official information disseminated by Tehran," without providing any further detail.
The Iranian Foreign Ministry renewed the regime's rejection on Thursday of longtime and widely held beliefs that Tehran materially supports the Houthi rebels fighting the Saudi Arabia-backed government in Yemen's decade-long civil war. The conflict intensified a couple months ago and quickly became the most active and deadly front in the intertwined conflicts in the Middle East.
Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called the latest accusation of Iranian support for the Houthis, made Monday by European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, "baseless," and said Iran "strongly denied claims that Iranian military experts were present in Yemen."
The U.S. government, along with many other Western nations and the NATO alliance , have demanded for years that Iran stop supporting the Houthis. The support, according to these nations, includes financial backing, weapons and other equipment, and direct coordination and training.

articles.title_orig: Bomb threats hit multiple flights in Europe for a second time in a week

articles.content_orig:

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Bomb threats across Europe have grounded flights across several countries and caused travel disruptions on Thursday.
It marks the second time this week that such widespread threats have been reported prompting fear and concern against the backdrop of a series of cyber-attacks affecting supermarket fridges and blood banks across the continent.
Flights flying to and from the UK , Belgium , Ireland, Italy , Finland , Bulgaria , Spain and Denmark were impacted and were largely resolved by the end of the day.
More than a dozen flights were targeted, included those from Copenhagen , Dublin , Helsinki , Madrid, Milan and Warsaw.
A Finnair plane from Helsinki was safely escorted to its scheduled landing in Rome by Italian Air Force jets. A Ryanair aircraft landed at Sofia airport after planes flying from Copenhagen and Madrid landed in the Bulgarian capital, according to the country’s interior minister.
Inspections of three Ryanair aircraft that received bomb threats and landed at the Bulgarian airports did not identify any issues, the country’s transport ministry said.
“Upon landing, the necessary inspections were carried out in accordance with the applicable procedures and no issues were identified,” the country’s transport ministry told Reuters. Airport operations at both Sofia and Plovdiv airports have returned to normal, it said.
Airports in the UK were also impacted amid threats reported at Heathrow and Birmingham airports.
“Threats reported at Heathrow and Birmingham in the early hours of this morning have been resolved,” a government spokesperson said in a statement issued on Thursday.
“It’s right that authorities treat any potential threats seriously — the UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any threats, as well as malicious hoaxes, like those we’ve seen this week.”
The Times reported that the Metropolitan Police are continuing to monitor the situation.
Finnair also said that its two affected flights had landed safely after being affected by bomb threats.
Flights AY1761 from Helsinki to Rome and AY1471 from Helsinki to Vienna, faced unfounded or hoax bomb threats, the company said.
“Both flights landed safely at their destinations, and customers have disembarked the aircraft,” it said and added that nothing suspicious was found on the planes.
The plane to Rome was inspected and will depart back to Helsinki, while the flight to Vienna will “return to traffic normally after inspection.”
The incidents followed hoax bomb threats earlier this week that prompted searches, diversions and, in one case, a military escort across at least seven flights in Europe. An airport in Poland was forced to close in a day of chaos on Tuesday.
“Malicious” bomb scares on two flights from London , and others from Manchester, Copenhagen, Israel , Dublin, Bergamo and Lisbon threw airports into disarray, with authorities searching planes after some of the flights were forced to undergo emergency landings.
Hundreds of passengers on board were affected as well as others who had been affected by the temporary closures of airports.
On Wednesday, the French health ministry said that blood banks in France had been hit by a cyberattack amid a series of online hoaxes and cyberattacks.
“Several regional facilities of the French Blood Establishment (EFS) were affected by a cybersecurity incident that impacted certain cold storage room monitoring and control systems,” the ministry said.
Meanwhile, stores in eight European countries were forced to throw away vast quantities of food after hackers tampered with their fridges on Monday, mirroring hacks that swept dozens of supermarkets in France three weeks ago.

articles.title_orig: Gamers go to ridiculous lengths to “improve” GTA VI with Nvidia’s DLSS 5
articles.title_zh: Gamers go to ridiculous lengths to “improve” GTA VI with Nvidia’s DLSS 5
articles.content_orig:
While the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI won’t be available on PC this month, some gamers are making ridiculous preparations to use their PC graphics cards to apply Nvidia’s DLSS 5 technology to the console exclusive.
On an explicitly unmoderated GTAVI subreddit, user RevolutionaryBus8208 lays out a proposed setup, which runs a PlayStation 5 through a 4K capture card to a PC. From there, the video signal is run through Veyra , an open source tool that can apply DLSS 5’s AI-powered “neural rendering” to video content. The result—which also uses DLSS frame generation to increase the 30 fps source to a 90 fps output—is then piped back to a 4K TV, theoretically adding some of the benefits of a beefy PC graphics card to a console-exclusive game.
To demonstrate the potential of this setup, RevolutionaryBus8208 used Veyra to upscale the Grand Theft Auto VI Extended Look trailer posted in August. The resulting DLSS-ified version looks a bit better in places, with sharper background elements, subtler shadows, and more believable light scattering on some surfaces. But it also seems a bit washed out compared to the original video’s deeper blacks and arguably suffers from an unnaturally smooth “soap opera effect” in some scenes.
While the upscaled version causes some occasional graphical artifacts and glitches from the frame generation process, it’s still an interesting proof of concept that shows just how far DLSS 5 has come from some of the early horror-show memes that circulated on the Internet earlier this year.
Of course, running this kind of remote frame generation on a linear video is very different from applying it to a real-time interactive game. While a pure “passthrough” capture card wouldn’t necessarily add any latency itself, any software processing done to get the video feed ready for upscaling—and to do the upscaling itself—could add significant delays between player inputs and on-screen results.
RevolutionaryBus8208 claims that Veyra itself adds a relatively small 11 ms of additional latency to the video source but admits he doesn’t have a capture card to test it with a signal coming from an actual PS5. Other commenters who have tried similar setups with other PS5 games said the input lag was “noticeable but tolerable” or claimed an impossible-to-believe latency addition of “around 1-2 milliseconds.”
For players who can already use Sony’s “PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution” on a PS5 Pro, going through this convoluted process might cause a “hat on a hat” effect. But for stock PS5 owners who happen to have a beefy PC GPU, the hassles and trade-offs might be worth it to get some additional horsepower on console exclusives like GTA VI .
Or, you know, you could just wait for the game’s actual PC release, which is reportedly slated for early 2027 . Or for the likely AI-assisted unofficial decompilation port that should be along any day now.

articles.content_orig:
Shift Up has launched a new live-action launch trailer for Stellar Blade: Complete Edition on Switch 2, and it's... well, we have so many questions.
To be fair, the message is clear: take EVE wherever you go, right? It's a nod toward the Switch 2's portable nature, though why EVE is interrupting someone's gaming session to brush their teeth is a bit odd now, isn't it?
We're also a bit puzzled as to why the ad goes for the 4:3 aspect ratio. It's not particularly cinematic or anything, so it doesn't make a whole lot of sense.
Despite our questions, however, it's a fun little ad. Harmless, y'know, and certainly a lot better than the AI-generated slop Shift Up posted to advertise its upcoming sequel.
Stellar Blade: Complete Edition is out now for the Switch 2. We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review, praising the combat and exploration, though noting that the visuals and performance aren't quite as good as we'd hoped.

A delegation of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV) led by Nguyen Thanh Nghi, member of the Political Bureau, Secretary of the CPV Central Committee, and head of the committee’s Commission for Policy and Strategy, paid a working visit to China from November 1 to 5. The visit followed the fifth plenary session of the 20th central committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC).
Nghi met with Wang Huning, member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC); held talks with He Lifeng, member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Vice Premier, and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Financial and Economic Affairs; and had a working session with Lu Hao, member of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Development Research Centre of the State Council of China.
He congratulated China on its tremendous and comprehensive development achievements and the success of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, held from October 26–29, describing it as an important theoretical preparation for the CPC’s 21st National Congress. He further expressed confidence that China would successfully implement the Resolution of the 20th National Congress of the CPC, successfully convene the 21st National Congress, and achieve its goal of building China into a modern socialist country that is prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful.
Nghi also briefed the Chinese side on the implementation of the resolution of Vietnam’s 14th National Party Congress and the country’s socio-economic development, as well as several key policies and orientations adopted at the fourth plenum of the Party Central Committee.
Highlighting the long-standing friendship between Vietnam and China and Vietnam’s policy of giving top priority to developing ties with China, he affirmed that the Vietnamese Party and State stand ready to work with their Chinese counterparts to further strengthen political trust, enhance strategic connectivity, elevate substantive cooperation and support each other in their respective development processes.
Appreciating the significance of the visit, which followed a series of exchanges and meetings between the two countries’ high-ranking leaders, the Chinese leaders affirmed that China always regards relations with Vietnam as a priority in its neighbourhood diplomacy and supports Vietnam in playing a greater international role.
The two sides spoke highly of the positive and comprehensive progress in Vietnam-China relations and agreed to strengthen the leadership and guidance of the two Parties over ministries, sectors, agencies and localities in both countries.
China welcomed Vietnam’s participation in its ‘Big Market for All: Export to China’ initiative. It also expressed readiness to further increase imports of Vietnamese agricultural products and support capable Chinese enterprises in expanding investment in Vietnam.
Following the talks in Beijing the delegation visited Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province.
